igbp.BSV: Barren Sparse Vegetation: Lands exposed soil, sand, or rocks and has less than 10% vegetative cover during any time of the year.
igbp.CRO: Croplands: Lands covered with temporary crops followed by harvest and a bare soil period (e.g., single and multiple cropping systems). Note that perennial woody crops will be classified as the appropriate forest or shrub land cover type.
igbp.CSH: Closed Shrublands: Lands with woody vegetation less than 2 meters tall and with shrub canopy cover >60%. The shrub foliage can be either evergreen or deciduous.
igbp.CVM: Cropland\/Natural Vegetation Mosaics: Lands with a mosaic of croplands, forest, shrublands, and grasslands in which no one component comprises more than 60% of the landscape
igbp.DBF: Deciduous Broadleaf Forests: Lands dominated by woody vegetation with a percent cover >60% and height exceeding 2 meters.  Consists of broadleaf tree communities with an annual cycle of leaf-on and leaf-off periods.
igbp.DNF: Deciduous Needleleaf Forests: Lands dominated by woody vegetation with a percent cover >60% and height exceeding 2 meters.  Consists of seasonal needleleaf tree communities with an annual cycle of leaf-on and leaf-off periods.
igbp.EBF: Evergreen Broadleaf Forests: Lands dominated by woody vegetation with a percent cover >60% and height exceeding 2 meters. Almost all trees and shrubs remain green year round. Canopy is never without green foliage.
igbp.ENF: Evergreen Needleleaf Forests: Lands dominated by woody vegetation with a percent cover >60% and height exceeding 2 meters. Almost all trees remain green all year. Canopy is never without green foliage.
igbp.GRA: Grasslands: Lands with herbaceous types of cover. Tree and shrub cover is less than 10%. Permanent wetlands lands with a permanent mixture of water and herbaceous or woody vegetation. The vegetation can be present in either salt, brackish, or fresh water.
igbp.MF: Mixed Forests: Lands dominated by trees with a percent cover >60% and height exceeding 2 meters.  Consists of tree communities with interspersed mixtures or mosaics of the other four forest types.  None of the forest types exceeds 60% of landscape.
igbp.OSH: Open Shrublands: Lands with woody vegetation less than 2 meters tall and with shrub canopy cover between 10-60%. The shrub foliage can be either evergreen or deciduous.
igbp.SAV: Savannas: Lands with herbaceous and other understory systems, and with forest canopy cover between 10-30%. The forest cover height exceeds 2 meters.
igbp.SNO: Snow and Ice: Lands under snow\/ice cover most of the year.
igbp.URB: Urban and Built-Up Lands: Land covered by buildings and other man-made structures.
igbp.WAT: Water Bodies : Oceans, seas, lakes, reservoirs, and rivers. Can be either fresh or salt- water bodies.
igbp.WET: Permanent Wetlands: Lands with a permanent mixture of water and herbaceous or woody vegetation that cover extensive areas. The vegetation can be present in either salt, brackish, or fresh water
igbp.WSA: Woody Savannas: Lands with herbaceous and other understory systems, and with forest canopy cover between 30-60%. The forest cover height exceeds 2 meters.

koeppen.Cfb: Marine West Coast: mild with no dry season, warm summer
koeppen.Cfc: Marine West Coast: mild with no dry season, cool summer
koeppen.Csa: Mediterranean: mild with dry, hot summer
koeppen.Csb: Mediterranean: mild with dry, warm summer
koeppen.Cwa: Humid Subtropical: dry winter, hot summer
koeppen.Cwb: Temperate Highland: dry winter, warm summer
koeppen.Cwc: Temperate Highland: dry winter, cool summer
koeppen.Dfa: Humid Continental: humid with severe winter, no dry season, hot summer
koeppen.Dfb: Warm Summer Continental: significant precipitation in all seasons
koeppen.Dfc: Subarctic: severe winter, no dry season, cool summer
koeppen.Dfd: Subarctic: severe, very cold winter, no dry season, cool summer
koeppen.Dsd: Subarctic: severe, very cold winter, dry cool summer
koeppen.Dwa: Humid Continental: humid with severe winter, no dry season, warm summer
koeppen.Dwc: Subarctic: severe, dry winter, cool summer
koeppen.Dwd: Subarctic: severe, very cold and dry winter, cool summer
